title: Henrietta Maria's household (Paris) to 'Sir' at the King's side, 26 January 1646, in Lasry's SP106-5 key: TNA SP 106/10 f. 247 (DECODE R929)

documents.route: Henrietta Maria's household, Paris -> 'Sir' (a correspondent with the King)

plaintext.source: George Lasry, reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-5' and interlinear plaintext of ff. 245-247 on the DECODE record, 23 Oct 2020

transcription.source: Sofia Pettersson's manual transcription (DECODE, 29 Oct 2019), raw file and as aligned in Lasry's interlinear file
transcription.notes: Image fetched with the DECODE cookie and viewed for the page crop (14 Oct 2026); the cipher is written sideways on the leaf. Transcription not redone.

system.summary: Lasry's 'TNA SP106-5' key (Jan 1646): a numerical homophonic alphabet of one- and two-digit values (up to five for E) with a nomenclator written as a letter and a digit (n3 the, k1 of, a1 and, e5 in ...) and a few three-digit numbers; numbers separated by colons.
system.sibling_key: Same key, per Lasry's files, on R928 (ff. 245-246, Dr Stephen Goffe at The Hague, January 1646); also the Charles I-Henrietta Maria key that read rupert1645 (Add MS 72438)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the former hm1645, which joined six letters in four of Lasry's keys. Lasry's key file says there are no nulls; the figures 81-90, which the key leaves without a value, fall between words, so nulls are left 'unknown' here. Other entries: hm1645 (TNA SP 106 key), sp106r787 (SP106-2), sp106r924 (SP106-8).

prior_solution.where: DECODE record files of R929 (George Lasry, 23 Oct 2020: reconstructed key, interlinear plaintext, dating notes)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: apply_key.py (key applied group by group to the transcription and compared with Lasry's plaintext)

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record page of R929 with the shared cookie; it links Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-5' and his plaintext of ff. 245-247 (2020-10-23).

Applied Lasry's SP106-5 alphabet to Pettersson's raw transcription of f. 247, independently of his plaintext file: it reads English ('... RECEIVED <425>S ... DECEMB ... IANVARY ... THANKES ... WEKLY ADVERTISEMENTS ... CONCERNING THE EMBASSAGE AND MARRIAGE') matching his plaintext.

Re-fetched the record files and applied the key group by group to all 348 groups of f. 247 (apply_key.py): 293 groups get a value, and all 293 equal Lasry's plaintext; 55 groups have no value in the key (17 distinct three-digit numbers, the figures 81-90 between words, e3).

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R929 is the only letter of the six in the SP106-5 key, and the only one where his key was applied here before his plaintext was compared. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's SP106-5 key (DECODE R929, 2020) was applied here to Pettersson's transcription of f. 247 without his plaintext; it gives 293 of 348 groups a value, all equal to his plaintext.
outcome.fraction_read_source: apply_key.py over decode/ (Pettersson's groups as aligned in Lasry's interlinear file): 293 of 348 cipher groups have a value in Lasry's SP106-5 key

gaps.item: three-digit nomenclator numbers (17 distinct, 23 tokens: 425, 199, 429, 810, 241 ...) and the letter-digit group e3 (2 tokens)
gaps.detail: Not in Lasry's key; most are names (241 is probably the King: 'the <241>s affaires'). Not reconstructed here.
Not in the key; they fall between words ('HOW _ BAD _ SO EUER'), so dividers or nulls, against the 'no nulls' of Lasry's key file. Not settled.

outcome.notes: Lasry's plaintext existed before the key was applied here; the application reproduces it group for group. The letter is signed 316 440 (Lasry's '<316> <440> <236>'). Sibling in the same key: R928 (ff. 245-246, Goffe from The Hague).
